block.prompt:
Write a discursive essay of 220–260 words on the following title:

**"Artificial intelligence will create more opportunities than problems for the next generation of workers."**

In your essay you should:
- discuss arguments for and against this statement
- use specific examples to support the points you make
- come to a clearly reasoned conclusion that gives your own view

Write in a formal, academic register. Use your planning grid from the previous task to guide your writing.
block.answer_key: Model answer: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has sparked intense debate about its effects on employment. While some fear widespread job losses, others argue that new technology has historically created as many opportunities as it has destroyed. On balance, the opportunities are likely to outweigh the problems — provided that societies invest in education and retraining. Those who see AI as an opportunity point to productivity gains and the creation of entirely new professions. The rise of machine learning has, for instance, generated demand for AI ethicists, data scientists, and prompt engineers — roles that did not exist a decade ago. Furthermore, AI can take over repetitive and dangerous tasks, freeing human workers to focus on creative, relational, and strategic work that machines struggle to replicate. However, the transition will not be painless. Workers in routine-based occupations — from lorry drivers to data-entry clerks — face genuine displacement risks, and without adequate retraining programmes, the burden will fall disproportionately on those least able to bear it. There is also a risk that productivity gains will be captured by companies rather than shared with workers. In conclusion, artificial intelligence is neither inherently good nor bad for employment; it is a powerful tool whose effects depend entirely on the policy choices societies make. With the right investment in lifelong learning and fair labour regulation, AI can indeed open more doors than it closes. (Auf Deutsch: Bewertet werden Aufbau, Argumentation, sprachliche Mittel und die Qualität der Schlussfolgerung — nicht die inhaltliche Position.)
block.acceptable_reasoning: Sowohl Pro- als auch Contra-Haltungen in der Schlussfolgerung sind akzeptabel; entscheidend ist die Nachvollziehbarkeit der Argumentation.

levels: Both sides discussed with specific examples; clear, reasoned personal conclusion; word count met
Both sides present but examples vague or personal conclusion weak; word count approximately met
One-sided or lacks personal conclusion; significantly over/under word count
Ideas logically sequenced; paragraphs well-developed; wide range of linking devices used accurately
Generally clear organisation; some linking devices but limited variety or occasional misuse
Poor paragraph structure; linking devices absent or used incorrectly
Wide, precise vocabulary; topic-specific terms used correctly; effective use of hedging language
Adequate vocabulary; some variety; minor inaccuracies that do not obscure meaning
Limited or repetitive vocabulary; frequent inappropriate word choices
Wide range of structures including complex sentences; errors rare and do not impede meaning
Mix of simple and complex structures; errors present but do not generally impede communication
Predominantly simple structures; frequent errors that impede meaning
Consistently formal academic register; adheres to discursive essay conventions throughout
Generally formal with occasional lapses; structure recognisable as a discursive essay
Register inconsistent; essay structure not clearly followed

watch_outs: Häufigster struktureller Fehler: Kein klarer Standpunkt in der Schlussfolgerung. Der Essay endet mit einer Auflistung von Argumenten ohne eigene Bewertung. Explizit einfordern.
Schüler:innen schreiben oft zwei isolierte Listen (pro / contra) ohne Verknüpfung. Auf Konnektoren und Übergangsformulierungen hinweisen (on the other hand, while it is true that, nevertheless …).
Wortanzahl: Schüler:innen schreiben entweder deutlich zu wenig (unter 180 Wörter) oder verlieren sich in unnötig langen Einleitungen. Die Zeit-Aufwand-Verteilung im Schreib-Prozess besprechen.
Register: informelle Formulierungen ('I think AI is cool', 'lots of jobs') in einem akademischen Essay sind typische Stilbrüche auf diesem Niveau.

Quellen und Beispiele: Es ist normal, keine verifizierbaren Quellen zu nennen — Formulierungen wie 'research suggests' oder 'studies indicate' sind akzeptabel, solange keine falschen Fakten behauptet werden.
